chunks.text: Today, we will talk about something very important, passports and visas.
If you want to travel to another country, you need a passport.
And in some cases, you also need a visa.
But what if you don't speak English very well?
How do you ask for a passport?
How do you apply for a visa?
Don't worry.
What is a passport?
A passport is an official document that allows you to travel to other countries.
It has your name, photo, nationality, and passport number.
If you don't have a passport, you cannot travel internationally.
Key vocabulary.
Passport, a travel document with your identity.
Application form, a document you fill out to apply.
Photo ID, a picture of your face.
Expiry date, the date when your passport is no longer valid.
Embassy, the office of a country in another country.
Immigration, the office that checks passports at the airport.
Example conversation.
Hello, I would like to apply for a passport.
Do you have your documents?
Yes, here they are.
Tip, always check your passport expiry date before traveling.
Some countries require at least six months of validity.
How to apply for a passport?
To get a new passport, you need to go to the passport office or apply online.
Common phrases to use at the passport office.
I need to apply for a passport.
What documents do I need?
How long does it take to get a passport?
How much does a passport cost?
Can I apply online?
Where can I take a passport photo?
Example conversation.
Excuse me, where can I apply for a passport?
You need to fill out an application form.
What documents do I need?
You need your ID, birth certificate, and a passport photo.
Tip, passport applications can take a few weeks, so apply early if you have travel plans.
Renewing an expired passport.
If your passport is expired, you need to renew it.
Common phrases when renewing a passport.
I need to renew my passport.
My passport expired last month.
How long does the renewal take?
Do I need to bring my old passport?
Example conversation.
Hello, my passport is expired.
How can I renew it?
You need to fill out this form and bring your old passport.
Okay, how long does it take?
It takes about two weeks.
Tip, some countries offer emergency passport services if you need one quickly.
What is a visa?
A visa is a special stamp or sticker in your passport that allows you to enter a country.
Some countries allow visa -free travel, but others require a visa before you travel.
Key vocabulary.
Tourist visa, a visa for short trips.
Work visa, a visa that allows you to work.
Student visa, a visa for studying in another country.
Visa application, the process of getting a visa.
Visa fee, the cost of a visa.
Interview, a meeting to check your visa application.
Example conversation.
Do I need a visa to visit the USA?
Yes, you need to apply for a tourist visa.
Tip, always check visa requirements before booking your flight.
How to apply for a visa?
When applying for a visa, you may need a passport, a visa application form, a passport photo, a bank statement to show you have enough money.
A return flight ticket.
Common phrases when applying for a visa.
How can I apply for a visa?
Do I need an interview?
What documents do I need for a visa?
How much does the visa fee?
Hello, I want to apply for a visa to Canada.
You need to fill out the application form and bring your passport.
Do I need an interview?
Yes, we will schedule an interview next week.
Tip, some visas take a long time to process, so apply going through immigration at the airport.
At the airport, you must show your passport and visa at immigration control.
Common phrases at immigration.
Here is my passport.
I am traveling for tourism.
I will stay for two weeks.
I have a return ticket.
I am staying at a hotel.
Immigration officer passport, please.
Here you go.
What is the purpose of your visit?
I am traveling for tourism.
How long will you stay?
Two weeks.
Tip, always answer clearly and honestly at immigration.
Now you know how to speak English when getting a passport or visa.
Final tips.
One, check passport expiry dates before traveling.
Two, prepare all necessary documents when applying for a passport or visa.
Three, be polite and confident when speaking English at embassies or immigration.
Four, arrive early for visa interviews and passport applications.
Five, always check travel requirements before booking a flight.
I hope this episode helps you feel confident when speaking English for passports and visas.
Thank you for listening.
If you enjoyed this episode, please subscribe to my podcast.
See you next time.
Bye -bye.
